chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah ibn Ayyūb, from ʿUmar ibn Abān al-Kalbī, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about nabīdh whose boiling had subsided, so he said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade al-dubbāʾ and al-muzaffat, and you added al-ghiḍār. Al-muzaffat means the pitch that is in the skin vessel, which is poured into the large jars so that it may be better suited for wine.”

key_terms.الدُّبَّاءِ: gourd containers that were prohibited for use in this context
key_terms.الزِّفْتَ: pitch or tar used in lining containers
key_terms.الْمُزَفَّتِ: a vessel coated or treated with pitch
key_terms.نَبِيذٍ: a fermented drink infusion under discussion in the hadith

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about nabīdh and the prohibition of al-dubbāʾ and al-muzaffat?
ai.summary: This hadith relates a ruling concerning nabīdh and cites a prohibition from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم regarding certain containers associated with fermentation. It clarifies the meaning of al-muzaffat as a vessel treated with pitch, indicating its connection to the preparation and preservation of intoxicants.
